info.title: beenfar
info.description:
REST binding of the beenfar controller API. The same operations are
available over Connect, gRPC and gRPC-Web at their protobuf service paths.

Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (see ApiTokenService) or
with the session cookie set by AuthService.Login.

healthy.description: Whether the adapter is running (built-in) or connected (external).

statusMessage.description: Last error reported by or about the adapter, if any.

connectTime.description: When the adapter started or last connected.

beenfar.admin.v1.Adapter.description: Adapter is a device adapter, such as the built-in UniFi adapter.

beenfar.admin.v1.AdapterKind.description: AdapterKind says where an adapter runs.

beenfar.admin.v1.ApiToken.description: ApiToken describes an issued bearer token. It never contains the secret.

beenfar.admin.v1.AuthMethod.description: AuthMethod is how a request was authenticated.

proxy.title: proxy
proxy.description:
Set when a trusted reverse proxy authenticates users. The UI shows no
 login form: an unauthenticated request means the proxy is misconfigured.

basicEnabled.description:
Whether HTTP Basic auth is accepted (always with API tokens as the

redirectUrl.description:
Where to send the browser next, e.g. the proxy's sign-out page or the

id.title: id
id.description: Stable provider id used in URLs, e.g. "corp".

loginUrl.title: login_url
loginUrl.description:
Relative URL that starts the login flow. Append ?redirect=<path> to

beenfar.admin.v1.OidcProvider.title: OidcProvider
beenfar.admin.v1.OidcProvider.description: OidcProvider is a configured OpenID Connect identity provider.

gcm.title: gcm
gcm.description:

 is encrypted, and the reply uses the same.

beenfar.admin.v1.UnifiDeviceKey.title: UnifiDeviceKey
beenfar.admin.v1.UnifiDeviceKey.description:
UnifiDeviceKey is the credential of one UniFi device, as extracted from the
 controller that manages it (its MongoDB "x_authkey", or "mgmt.authkey" in
 the device's /var/etc/persisted/cfg/mgmt).

admin.title: admin
admin.description:
Admins may manage users, every API token and adapters. For external
 users whose provider maps groups to admin, this is derived from their
 groups at each sign-in and cannot be changed here.

locked.title: locked
locked.description:
The device was seen but its adapter holds no credentials for it, so it
 cannot be adopted yet (for UniFi: it is still managed by another
 controller). Import its credentials, or reset it, and it stops being
 locked the next time it is seen.

readoption.title: readoption
readoption.description: Set while an adopted device that was reset is being adopted again.

forgetting.title: forgetting
forgetting.description:
Set while the device is being forgotten and the controller is waiting for
 it to reset itself (see ForgetDevice). The device is removed once it has.

kind.description: What the device is, as far as its adapter can tell.

portCount.title: port_count
portCount.description:
How many ports beyond the uplink can be configured with
 beenfar.config.v1.SwitchPortService. Most access points have none, so a
 client should offer port settings only when this is above zero. Zero for
 a device whose kind is unspecified means "not known", and port settings
 are accepted.

 UpdateDevice).

beenfar.config.v1.DeviceSettings.description: DeviceSettings are the settings of a device an operator can change.

beenfar.config.v1.FieldWriter.title: FieldWriter
beenfar.config.v1.FieldWriter.description:
FieldWriter says who last set one field of a resource, and when.

 It is a record of writes, not a claim of ownership: beenfar cannot know
 that a client "manages" a field, only that the client named it in a create
 or in the update_mask of an update. Clients that send only the fields they
 manage, as the Terraform provider and the UI do, are recorded for exactly
 those fields. Fields nobody has written since this was recorded have no
 entry.

beenfar.config.v1.FieldWriterKind.description: FieldWriterKind says what kind of caller wrote a field.

get.description: ListAdapters returns every registered adapter, ordered by name.

post.description:
ImportUnifiDeviceKeys stores the credentials of UniFi devices that
 another controller manages, so that this controller can read their
 informs once they are pointed at it. The devices are recorded as pending
 (with their real model once they have informed) and are adopted, which
 re-keys them, like any other. The keys are never returned by any API.

get.description: ListApiTokens lists the caller's tokens, or every token for an admin.

post.description:
CreateApiToken issues a token for the calling user. The secret is
 returned only in this response; the server keeps only its hash.

get.description:
GetAuthConfig describes the sign-in methods this controller offers, so a
 UI can render the right login screen. It needs no credentials.

post.description:
Login checks a username and password and starts a session. The response
 sets an HttpOnly session cookie. Fails with UNAUTHENTICATED on bad
 credentials.

Logout ends the current session and clears the cookie. When the user
 signed in through an external provider, redirect_url is where the UI
 should send the browser to sign out there too.

get.description: GetCurrentUser returns the user behind the caller's session or token.

put.description:
UpdateDevice changes the operator-set settings of a device: for now only
 ap_group, which pins an access point to one AP group. The access point
 then broadcasts the wifi networks that are not limited to named groups
 plus those that list its group, and not the ones limited to other groups;
 with no group it broadcasts every network. Only access points take an
 ap_group.
 Fields named by update_mask are replaced; an empty mask replaces all of
 them. All other fields are output only and ignored.

get.description: GetDevice returns one device by id.

delete.description:
ForgetDevice stops managing a device. An adopted device is factory reset
 (for UniFi: told to reset itself on its next inform), so that it comes back
 as a new, pending device that can be adopted again. The reset can only be
 delivered when the device next contacts the controller, so until then the
 device stays in the list with forgetting set, and is removed once it has
 reset; asking again meanwhile changes nothing, and force gives up waiting
 and removes it at once without resetting it (the device then still holds
 the key beenfar threw away, so it must be reset by hand before it can be
 adopted: it shows as locked). A pending or locked device has nothing to
 reset and is removed at once.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description:
Remove the device now instead of waiting for it to reset itself. Over REST:
 DELETE /api/v1/devices/{id}?force=true.

get.description:
GetDeviceSettings returns the settings an operator can change on a device,
 both the original ones and the current ones. The names and meaning of the
 settings belong to the device's adapter; for a UniFi access point of a
 supported model they are its radio settings (channel, width, power, ...).
 A device whose model has none returns both maps empty.

patch.description:
UpdateDeviceSettings sets some of a device's current settings: the keys in
 the request replace the current values and the other keys are kept. A key
 the device's model does not have, or a value it does not accept, fails
 with INVALID_ARGUMENT and changes nothing. It fails with
 FAILED_PRECONDITION for a device that is not adopted or whose model has no
 settings. The device is sent the new settings the next time it informs.

current.title: current
current.description: The settings to set, by key. Keys not listed keep their current value.

post.description:
ResetDeviceSettings returns a device's current settings to its original
 ones.

AdoptDevice brings a pending device under management, or accepts the
 re-adoption of an adopted device whose readoption is AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE.
 It fails with NOT_FOUND if no such device has been seen and
 FAILED_PRECONDITION if it is already adopted and not awaiting.

tags.name: AdapterService
tags.description: AdapterService reports the device adapters registered with the controller.

tags.name: ApiTokenService
tags.description:
ApiTokenService manages bearer tokens for programmatic access (Terraform,
 scripts). A token acts as the user who created it. Users see and revoke
 their own tokens; admins see and revoke everyone's.

tags.name: UserService
tags.description:
UserService manages controller users. Only admins may call it, except that
 any user may read their own record and change their own password.

tags.name: AuthService
tags.description:
AuthService signs browser users in and out with a session cookie. API
 clients use bearer tokens from ApiTokenService instead.

tags.name: DeviceService
tags.description:
DeviceService manages network devices: discovery results, adoption and
 removal. Devices are created by adapters when they are first seen, in the
 PENDING state; AdoptDevice brings one under management.

tags.name: NetworkService
tags.description: NetworkService manages wired/L3 networks (VLANs and their subnets).

tags.name: RadiusServerService
tags.description:
RadiusServerService manages the RADIUS servers that WPA-enterprise
 wireless networks authenticate against.
